question.problem: A computer program is designed so that it can randomly generate a real number between $0$ and $10,$ inclusive. What is the probability that the number generated is between $3$ and $7?$

current_example.problem: The duration of a radio program is uniformly distributed between $27$ and $34$ minutes, inclusive. What is the probability that a randomly chosen program lasts less than $30$ minutes?
current_example.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the duration of the radio program. From the problem statement, we know that $X \sim U[27,34],$ and we wish to compute $P(X < 30).$

In general, if $X \sim U[a,b],$ then $X$ has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14214230/assets/a3fbd3c99057274252e6ced7d514965080377c29a5c225e395af8fe04f4ab5e6.svg)

So, for our random variable $X \sim U[27,34],$ we have the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14214230/assets/ac610bb89bfa4bed8297facdda370509d52cd2654aa5f353ffd35f14e13e3660.svg)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<30) & ={\int }_{27}^{30}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{27}^{30}\frac{1}{7}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{x}{7}|}_{27}^{30} \\  & =\frac{30}{7}-\frac{27}{7} \\  & =\frac{3}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
